title: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) · Paper 2 — original full-length mock (non-calculator)
subject: cambridge-igcse-mathematics-0580
instructions: Original full-length practice: 24 questions, 100 marks. This is not an official or endorsed Cambridge examination. Answer every question and all parts. Show your reasoning and calculations in the working canvas beneath each question; add pages when needed. Calculators are not permitted. Give exact answers unless a question specifies an approximation. Formula facts are attached to every question. Draw and label your own axes where requested; one grid square may represent the scale stated in the question. Use straight ruled lines and smooth curves as appropriate. Dimensions stated in a question are exact unless described as rounded. There is no separate reading period.

resources.label: Extended formula facts
resources.text:
Mathematical formula facts — independently typeset for this practice paper
Triangle: area = bh/2 (b is the base, h the perpendicular height).
Circle: area = πr²; circumference = 2πr (r is the radius).
Cylinder: curved surface area = 2πrh; volume = πr²h.
Cone: curved surface area = πrl; volume = πr²h/3 (l is slant height; h is perpendicular height).
Sphere: surface area = 4πr²; volume = 4πr³/3.
Prism: volume = cross-sectional area × length.
Pyramid: volume = base area × perpendicular height / 3.
If ax² + bx + c = 0 and a ≠ 0: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a).
In a triangle with sides a, b, c opposite angles A, B, C:
a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C;
a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A;
area = ab sin C / 2.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.prompt: Work out 7/12 + 5/18, giving your answer as a fraction in its simplest form. Show your working. [2]

questions.label: Question 2
questions.prompt: Calculate (4.8 × 10⁷ × 2.5 × 10⁻³)/(6 × 10²). Give the answer in standard form. [3]

questions.label: Question 3
questions.prompt: The decimal 0.272727… has 27 recurring indefinitely. Show algebraically that it is equal to 3/11. [3]

questions.label: Question 4
questions.prompt:
(a) Simplify 3√50 − √8. [2]
(b) Rationalise the denominator of 1/√2. [1]

questions.label: Question 5
questions.prompt: After a 15% increase, an annual membership costs $92. Find its cost before the increase. Show your method. [3]

questions.label: Question 6
questions.prompt: For positive a and b, simplify (16a⁸b⁻⁴)^(1/2). Give your answer with positive indices. [3]

questions.label: Question 7
questions.prompt:
The universal set is the integers from 1 to 20 inclusive. A is the set of multiples of 3 and B is the set of factors of 18.
(a) List A ∩ B. [1]
(b) Find n(A ∪ B). [1]
(c) Find n((A ∪ B)′). [1]

questions.label: Question 8
questions.prompt: Simplify (x² − 9)/(x² + x − 6). State all values of x excluded from the original expression. [4]

questions.label: Question 9
questions.prompt: Solve 2x + 3y = 13 and 5x − 2y = 4. Show your working. [4]

questions.label: Question 10
questions.prompt: Solve 2x² − 7x − 4 = 0 by factorisation. [4]

questions.label: Question 11
questions.prompt: On a square grid, draw labelled axes covering −1 ≤ x ≤ 6 and −1 ≤ y ≤ 6. Show the region R satisfying x ≥ 0, y ≥ 1 and x + y ≤ 5. Shade the unwanted regions and label R. [4]

questions.label: Question 12
questions.prompt:
f(x)=3x−2 and g(x)=x²+1.
(a) Find g(f(x)), simplifying your expression. [2]
(b) Find f⁻¹(x). [2]

questions.label: Question 13
questions.prompt:
The first four terms of a quadratic sequence are 2, 7, 14, 23.
(a) Find its nth term. [3]
(b) Find its 10th term. [1]

questions.label: Question 14
questions.prompt:
A is (−2,1) and B is (4,9).
(a) Find the exact length AB. [2]
(b) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB. [2]

questions.label: Question 15
questions.prompt:
A, B, C and D lie on a circle in that order. Angle ABC is 72° and angle BAC is 31°.
(a) Find angle ADC, giving a reason. [2]
(b) Find angle BDC, giving a reason. [2]

questions.label: Question 16
questions.prompt:
(a) Solve 2 sin x = √3 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°. [3]
(b) A right-angled triangle has two angles of 45° and a hypotenuse of 10 cm. Find the exact length of either shorter side. [2]

questions.label: Question 17
questions.prompt:
A solid consists of a cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 8 cm, with a hemisphere of radius 3 cm attached to its top. Its bottom is a flat circular face.
(a) Find the total external surface area in terms of π. [3]
(b) Find the total volume in terms of π. [2]

questions.label: Question 18
questions.prompt:
Triangle ABC has vertices A(1,1), B(3,1), C(1,2).
(a) Rotate ABC through 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Draw and label the image on a grid. [3]
(b) In a separate transformation, enlarge the original triangle by scale factor −2 about the origin. Give the coordinates of the image of A and explain the effect of the negative sign. [2]

questions.label: Question 19
questions.prompt:
A bag contains 4 red, 3 blue and 2 green counters. Two are chosen at random without replacement.
(a) Find the probability that both have the same colour. [3]
(b) Given that the first counter is not red, find the probability that the second counter is red. [2]

questions.label: Question 20
questions.prompt:
Parcel masses m kg have this distribution:
0 < m ≤ 5: frequency 10
5 < m ≤ 15: frequency 30
15 < m ≤ 30: frequency 15
(a) Calculate the frequency density of each class. [2]
(b) Draw a histogram with labelled mass and frequency-density axes. [2]
(c) Find the proportion of parcels with mass at most 15 kg. [1]

questions.label: Question 21
questions.prompt:
The times t minutes taken by 40 students to complete a puzzle are:
0 < t ≤ 10: 4 students
10 < t ≤ 20: 8 students
20 < t ≤ 30: 16 students
30 < t ≤ 40: 12 students
(a) Make a cumulative-frequency table. [1]
(b) Draw a cumulative-frequency graph, including (0,0). [2]
(c) Use the graph to estimate the median time. [1]
(d) How many students took more than 30 minutes? [1]

questions.label: Question 22
questions.prompt:
In triangle OAB, OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB. N lies on OB with ON:NB = 2:1. The lines OM and AN meet at P.
(a) Express OM and AN in terms of a and b. [2]
(b) By comparing coefficients, find OP in terms of a and b. [3]
(c) State OP:PM. [1]

questions.label: Question 23
questions.prompt:
The curve is y = x³ − 6x² + 9x.
(a) Find dy/dx. [2]
(b) Find the coordinates of its two stationary points. [2]
(c) Determine whether each is a maximum or a minimum, giving reasons. [2]

questions.label: Question 24
questions.prompt:
A rectangle has length (x + 5) cm and width (x − 1) cm. Its area is 45 cm².
(a) Form a quadratic equation in x and simplify it. [2]
(b) Solve it, giving exact values, and explain which value is valid for the rectangle. [3]
(c) Find the exact perimeter of the rectangle. [1]
